judgments.reasoning_cat1: A holdover provision for the 'status quo' and 'alternate status quo' arbitrators, terms not used in Section 16 itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-G states that the term of the permanent impartial chairmen ends upon expiration of the Agreement, whereas this letter has incumbents serve until a replacement assumes office.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise holdover rule for the existing arbitrator list keyed to acceptance by new arbitrators.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-E.2 requires the parties to meet 'immediately after the execution of this Agreement' to select fifteen arbitrators, which this letter effectively postpones.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Weekly or bi-weekly basis as the Union may choose' with a sixty-day notice trigger is stated precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-N.1 requires deduction from the second pay check of each month, which this letter promises to amend on notice — an anticipated, but real, displacement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Times is happy to continue our discussions' is courtesy language creating no obligation, and 'Company' and 'The Times' are used interchangeably.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 17-D says the parties have bargained and settled terms for the term of the Agreement, which sits against continuing discussion of pension changes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Times has agreed to discussion concerning the feasibility' is an agreement to discuss only, and the condition 'providing such transport did not involve the Times in increased costs' appears only in the description of the Union's proposal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9-B uses the same increased-cost qualification for bulk deliveries by unit employees, so the letter tracks an existing standard without resolving it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If a sufficient number of employees are interested' and 'another acceptable bank' leave both the trigger and the counterparty undetermined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Credit Union Checkoff letter and 2-N.1 establish deduction machinery, which this program would use; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The equipment commitments are itemised and concrete, though 'all other long runs' is a general catch-all after two specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-H.1 requires all motor vehicles to be equipped with heaters and defrosters within thirty days, whereas this letter promises only that existing under-the-seat heaters be maintained and new trucks be equipped.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'When the six payments referred to in the Memorandum have been made' misdescribes the Memorandum, which refers to a six-month review rather than six payments, and 'under any circumstances' is absolute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Memorandum of Understanding requires payment of the full $177,844 in $1,250 monthly instalments and accelerates the balance on violation, which cannot stand with forgiveness after six payments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The extracted text is scrambled, with the closing and signature appearing before the substantive commitments, and 'the 48 inch height from the top of the skid' is stated without context.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D.VIII says the Newspoint agreement supersedes all other agreements relating to Newspoint, while this letter promises to abide by 'all Newspoint written agreements'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It revives a memorandum expressly deleted from the Agreement 'should there be a problem in the future arising thereunder' — a self-contradictory deletion, and the memorandum's content is not reproduced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Continuation of Side Agreements memorandum says every side agreement is continued and deemed updated, which is hard to reconcile with a deletion that nonetheless remains applicable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It promises to post rules of eligibility for 'the Medill Plan', a plan named nowhere else in the instrument, and states no substantive eligibility standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-H and 13-I establish the Welfare and Pension Funds with their own eligibility structures, so an unexplained third plan sits alongside them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A reasonable period of time designated by the employee' and 'a written assignment satisfactory to the Publisher' leave both duration and form to be settled later.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-N.1 and 2-N.3 govern dues and agency-fee deductions on comparable terms; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prohibits the subcontracting of bargaining unit deliveries except as it may exist pursuant to the contract' is circular — the exception is defined by the very instrument the letter purports to clarify.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-E freezes methods and extent, 3-F frees the Publisher on new routes, 2-E.2(d)/(h) permit expanded use of over-the-road carriers and 9-B contemplates outside printing, so what the contract 'permits' is exactly what is in dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Will continue its present practice' is undated, but the annual shift-statement obligation is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-I.1 makes contributions turn on shifts worked, so an annual statement of 'shifts to be credited' is the reporting counterpart of that formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Most obligations are conditioned on an undated future event ('when the planned DEC System is installed and operational'), and one paragraph refers to shifts 'for which contributions were not made' without saying why they were not.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-I.1 requires contributions for each shift worked capped at five per week, so a statement of credited shifts for which contributions were not made presupposes a gap this letter does not explain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except if delayed because of an emergency or Act of God' is a general excuse appended to a precise thirty-day deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-A.1 makes the first-year increase effective March 31, 1981 while the Agreement was executed in October 1981, which is why retroactivity is needed; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Incident to the negotiation of the present Collective Bargaining Committee' is nonsensical as written and the letter is dated November 3, 1978.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 1978 date makes this a prior-round document carried forward by the Continuation of Side Agreements memorandum, whose 'deemed updated' language leaves its current content uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Union requested ... and was advised that such vans would be ordered' records a statement rather than creating a promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-K requires the Publisher to furnish all delivery equipment, which this narrative does not add to; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Would explore the purchase and use of dehumidifiers' is an agreement to consider, imposing no ascertainable duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-H.1 requires protection against adverse weather exposure 'insofar as practicable', an equally soft standard covering similar ground.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Paid the same as the men in the New York plant for handling three-part inserts (500 or more)' is precise as to trigger and comparator.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-A sets uniform wage scales across Publishers, so a plant-to-plant parity rule for a task is a narrow supplement rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Company indicated that new trucks had been ordered' is a record of a statement, not an obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Heaters and Safety Equipment letter imposes actual equipment obligations on new trucks, which this narrative merely anticipates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sixers' is an undefined trade term and the commitment is measured by 'the same percentage as they are currently available' to another shift, an undated benchmark.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument defines 'sixers' or fixes the day-shift percentage, so the obligation cannot be sized from the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Five jobs would be defined when posted' names the jobs but says nothing about what the definitions must contain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B and 21-D.VII require posting of situations, and the posting letter adds job descriptions, so the mechanics are supplied elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement 'to meet and discuss' with no subject-matter standard or deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D.V governs commercial work at Newspoint, so the topic is already addressed in part; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A thirty-day meeting commitment on undefined 'shop level problems'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-A requires plant-level settlement attempts before referral, so a shop-level meeting duty is consistent with that structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble is garbled ('negotiation of the present Collective Bargaining Committee') and the heading appears at the end of the extract; it is dated November 3, 1978.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Carried into a 1981-84 agreement by the Continuation memorandum, whose 'deemed updated' formula leaves the operative status of these 1978 items unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise commitment to create two console jobs, one day and one night.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's Control Room clause requires delivery department console personnel to be journeymen, and Supplementary Agreement ¶1 adds utility men, all consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Days, start time and bidding method are all specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B governs the posting and filling of new situations, and inter-shop bidding is used elsewhere in Section 22; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Will be reviewed within a reasonable time ... but in no event later than sixty (60) days' commits only to a review, with no standard for its outcome.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Agreement ¶3 fixes combined floor hires at 81 between both plants, which supplies content this open review does not.
